arcadia-arcadia-1910-08-02.A1:
RACE RIOT
AVERTED
Special to the Express.

Special to the Express.
Oklahoma City, Aug. 3.—A race riot was narrowly averted at Arcadia, twenty-five miles northeast of here yesterday afternoon by the prompt action of an election inspector when 30 negroes lined up at the polls and refused to allow democrats to vote. The crowd was dispersed by the inspector drawing a revolver and threatening to shoot.
The trouble came when the election ballots for the republicans were all used up. The negroes sought to prevent the democrats from voting until they got their ballots to continue their voting. The polls were closed at 2:30 until more ballots could be obtained from the state election board.

john-loyelace-woodbury-1910-08.A2:
WHITE MEN
Accused of Robbing Two Georgia Negroes Shoot Them to Death.

Woodbury, Ga., August 10.—Because they accused a white man of stealing corn of them, two Negroes, John Lovelace and son, Edward, were shot to death late this afternoon by a crowd of infuriated whites.

The Negroes were prosperous farmers. They circulated reports that corn had been stolen from them by a member of a prominent family. This afternoon the man, with his four brothers and several other white men, went to the house of the Negroes to punish them for circulating the reports. The Negroes were seized by the whites and asked to retract the reports. This they refused to do, and, it is said, prepared to defend themselves. The whites at once opened fire and riddled the Negroes with bullets, the latter falling dead almost at their doorsteps.

[Special to The Times-Dispatch.]
Lynchburg, Va., August 13.—William Watkins, colored, lies probably mortally wounded at the City Hospital, his wound having been inflicted late last night by Policeman Kelly, as he was endeavoring to elude arrest for snatching a money purse from Mrs. J. H. Poole, who was sitting in front of her home on Twelfth Street. Wonder is expressed that the negro has lived this long, and he can hardly survive.
lynchburg-lynchburg-1910-08-12.A2:
Policeman Shoots Negro.
LYNCHBURG, VA., Aug. 13.—William Watkins, colored, is dying at the City Hospital from a revolver wound inflicted last night by Police man Kelly when the negro was trying to elude arrest for snatching a pocketbook from a white woman on Twelfth street. The negro was located after a long chase, and as he tried to run the officer fired. He was struck in the back and he cannot live. The negro admitted the robbery.
lynchburg-lynchburg-1910-08-12.A3:
Alleged Robber in Jail.
LYNCHBURG, Aug. 20. William Watkins, the negro who was shot 10 days ago while attempting to escape after snatching a money purse from a white woman, is now in the city jail, having been discharged from the City Hospital. The negro will go on trial shortly for highway robbery.
lynchburg-lynchburg-1910-08-12.A4:
WOUNDED NEGRO SENT ON TO GRAND JURY
LYNCHBURG, VA., Sept. 2.—Will Atkins, the negro who was badly shot by a policeman here several weeks ago, while attempting to elude arrest for snatching a purse from a lady on the street, was to-day sent to the grand jury by Mayor Smith in the Police Court.

shep-johnson-washington-1910-08-17.A1:
ATTEMPTS SUICIDE
AT STREET CORNER
Lynching Threatened in Southwest When Shot Is Fired.
William Javins stood at the corner of Thirteenth and C streets southwest about 10:30 o'clock this morning, placed the muzzle of a .38-caliber revolver in his mouth, and pulled the trigger.

Instead of producing instant death, as is usually the case when a revolver is discharged between the lips, the bullet drove four of the man's teeth into the left side of the upper jaw and flattened itself against the bone. Javins was taken to the Emergency Hospital, where the teeth and piece of lead were picked out. The surgeons were surprised to find that the man had not been seriously wounded.

Javins had just come out of the store of Philip A. Shea, 1300 C street, where he had delivered a freezer of icecream, and was standing on the curb when he tried to end his life.

The shooting caused the greatest excitement in the neighborhood, while a fleeing negro, who was innocently trying to keep out of trouble, added to the confusion. For a few minutes it looked as if the negro would be handled pretty roughly by the crowd.

"Shep" Johnson, the negro, was walking up C street carrying a string of fish, which he had just purchased at the fish wharf, and was not five feet from Javins when the shot was fired. Johnson is not familiar with the game and fish laws of the District. The first thought that came to his mind was that maybe it was the closed season and a vigilant game warden had fired the shot at him.

Naturally, Shep dropped the string of fish and "hit the grit." Persons who were in the neighborhood and heard the shot started after the negro. Somebody yelled, "There he goes; he did it," and the next moment the crowd was on Shep's heels. Seeing that it was no use to attempt to get away, Shep stopped running, and the crowd soon hemimed him in. Not knowing what had really occurred, the negro, trembling at the knees, began to plead with the crowd.

"Deed, boss, I didnt know it was agin the law to catch dem fish. No, sur; deed, sur, I didnt know."

Just then Policeman Bartemann, of the Fourth precinct, who had witnessed the attempted suicide and tried to prevent Javins from firing the shot, stepped up and explained that the negro had no hand in the affair.

Shep gathered up what remained of the string of fish and didn't waste any time getting away.

At the offices of his employers it was said Javins had threatened to kill him self about a year ago.

At the hospital he declined to tell the doctors why he had tried to commit suicide. He is twenty-six years old and lives at 349 N street southwest. He will recover.

shep-johnson-washington-1910-08-17.A4:
SHOOTS OUT TEETH.
William Javins Fails in Attempt to End His Life.
Placing the muzzle of a .38-caliber revolver in his mouth, William Javins, twenty-six years old, yesterday attempted to end his life while standing at Thirteenth and S streets southwest. His alm was bad, and the damage was the loss of four teeth and considerable blood. He was taken to Emergency Hospital, The bullet, which had flattended against the upper jaw bone, was extracted.

Javins, who is a helper on an ice cream delivery wagon, refused to tell the police why he had attempted suicide, but relatives say that the recent marriage of a girl to whom he had been attentive caused his despondency. He lives at 340 M street southwest. Physicians stated last night that his condition was not serious.
